newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker, but seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker, but seen consolidating.

text.p: COMEX copper ended slightly weaker after a choppy session but the market continued to consolidate within its recent trading range, traders said.

The market was basing but players were still a little long, therefore some nervous selling was seen on the back of the drop in equities and the rise in interest rates, Mike Frawley of Dean Witter said.
May COMEX settled 0.10 cent weaker at 111.55 cents a pound, traded 112.20 to 110.65. Spot April went out 0.25 cent lower at 112.60 cents. Volume was estimated at 9,000 lots.

Copper's fundamentals remained quite positive, with a lot of interest in Singapore warrants and good demand for red metal in the Far East against a background of some production problems in the U.S., Frawley added.
"I would view a pullback from current levels as a buying opportunity," Frawley said.
